en: The Ritual Manual for Recitation of the *Sūtra on the Meritorious Virtues of the Fundamental Vows of the Seven Buddhas,
the Medicine Master Vaidūryaprabharāja*, Volume One,
composed by the Venerable Sādhupāla.
Translated by the Tripitaka Śramaṇa Śālarabha of the Great Yuan, by Imperial Decree. Homage to the Tathāgata Bhaisajyaguru-vaiḍūryaprabharāja.
Those who practice this ritual manual shall bathe and purify themselves.
Wearing fresh and exquisite garments and partaking of pure food,
with a stainless and pure mind free from afflictions,
one contemplates and recollects the merits of the Triple Gem and the merits of the sutras.
Having generated sincere faith in the Truths, one cultivates the contemplation of the four immeasurables.
If one is a layperson, one should observe the eightfold fast-day precepts (*upavāsa-śīla*) on auspicious occasions,
such as the eighth day of the month.
Establish the site of practice (*dharmapūjā*) in a pleasing location, sweeping it clean and making it pure.
Adorn it with various banners, streamers, and parasols,
and using powdered incense or scattered flowers, establish a great altar of fragrance.
Within [the hall], one should install cast, poured, painted, or sculpted images of Śāriputra,
as well as arrange the seats for all the worldly and transcendental honored ones and holy sages,
and present various kinds of offerings according to one's ability.
Before each image, place seven lamps;
hang seven multi-colored silk banners;
and offer various superior kinds of burning incense, famous flowers, fragrant unguents, and exquisite food.
Various musical instruments, the seven treasures, the eight auspicious symbols, the precious vase, and so forth,
should all be prepared in advance according to one's means.
One should then command the monastic community to recite this sutra, the Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, the Vaipulya Sūtras, and others.
Whether for one week, three weeks, five weeks, or up to seven weeks,
one should construct a *maṇḍala*, perform recitations, and practice;
once such offerings have been thus prepared and displayed.
Having gathered the great assembly, he remained composed and orderly.
He cultivated the contemplation of the emptiness of intrinsic nature and arose from meditative absorption.
Then, taking all sentient beings as his object, he cultivated the contemplation of the four immeasurables.
Once the generation of the bodhicitta has been cultivated and accomplished,
one should likewise visualize all the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas of the ten directions as doing the same.
Regarding such contemplation and empowerment, the locus of empowerment and reception is called "the true power of the Three Jewels."
The power of the empowerment and sustenance of all Buddhas and great Bodhisattvas;
the power of the fruition of the perfection of the two types of provisions;
and the power of the inconceivable, pure Dharmadhātu.
The most wondrous and vast pure land,
accomplished through the vows of that Buddha and his Bodhisattvas,
is now [to be established] according to the ritual procedures found in the *Saptabuddhaka-pūrvapraṇidhāna-guṇa-dharma-sūtra*.
He assembled all the Buddhas of the ten directions, the great Bodhisattvas,
and the assembly of holy beings who protect the Dharma,
along with their palaces, maṇḍalas, and all manner of offerings and adornments of the buddha-fields.
I only pray that it may be transformed so as to be like the adornments of the land of the World-Honored One Amitāyus Buddha,
such that its various merits are equal and without difference.
The ground of that buddha-land shall be as level as the palm of a hand.
Composed of various jewels, it was perfectly square in length and breadth, vast, magnificent, fine, smooth, and exceedingly delightful;
it was pure and stainless, with a brilliant, dazzling radiance.
The fragrance was as exquisite as that of fine sandalwood.
Various kinds of sublime celestial flowers were scattered everywhere.
There were many bathing pools, their floors paved throughout with various wonderful jewels.
Furthermore, its bottom was strewn with various kinds of gold, silver, pearls, and exquisite jewels;
there were also various kinds of *utpala*, *kubjaka*, and *padma* flowers.
Glistening and lush, they lean and spread over the top.
Furthermore, there are various wondrous and lovely birds of diverse colors that emit harmonious and elegant sounds, bringing delight to the minds of all.
Filled with mutual joy, they soar and fly up and down.
Furthermore, various exquisite celestial jewels adorn the ponds and pools,
which are filled and overflowing with water endowed with the eight virtues.
It is pure, magnificent, and exceedingly delightful.
Furthermore, there are various kinds of celestial, wondrous jewel-trees;
each jewel-tree bears various kinds of jewel-flowers and jewel-fruits.
Lush and flourishing, they were adorned with railings arranged in rows everywhere;
upon each branch hung various celestial, exquisite pearl necklaces and clusters of mani jewels.
Golden jewel bells and chimes resounded spontaneously without being struck,
emitting exquisite sounds that proclaimed the sublime Dharma.
Such were the various adornments of the jeweled ground.
That supreme and wondrous palace was adorned and interspersed with the seven treasures;
its brilliant radiance blazed forth, illuminating immeasurable worlds throughout the ten directions,
such that the lands of the ten directions all appeared within it.
There are such immeasurable lands,
equal in length and breadth with distinct boundaries;
each is magnificently adorned, beyond the realm of the three worlds, and transcends the mundane world.
This is accomplished through the purification of the nature of consciousness by the power of the Tathāgata’s roots of goodness.
It is the abode of the Tathāgata and the assembly of immeasurable great bodhisattvas and others.
Furthermore, the devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras,
mahoragas, humans, non-humans, and others constantly traverse this place,
delighting in and enjoying the flavor of the Dharma, dwelling in peace, stability, and happiness.
Truly and constantly abiding in the benefit of sentient beings,
they remain far removed from defilements, grief, sorrow,
and affliction; forever free from demonic activities, they surpass all forms of adornment.
The Tathāgata’s adornment of city gates, towers,
and palaces is produced by great mindfulness, wisdom, and resolute understanding,
and is mounted upon śamatha and vipaśyanā.
He entered the universal gate of liberation of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness.
Within a great precious palace adorned with immeasurable and boundless merits by means of exquisite jewel-flower kings,
he sat upon a lion throne of various jewels atop a lotus flower.
The Tathāgata King of Auspicious Renown;
the Tathāgata Sovereign King of Jewel Moon, Wisdom Adornment, and Radiant Sound;
and the Tathāgata Accomplishment of Golden Jewel Light and Sublime Conduct.
The Tathāgata Aśokaśrīparamavijaya,
the Tathāgata Dharmasāgaragarjitasvara,
and the Tathāgata Dharmasāgaravarabuddhivikrīḍitābhijña.
The Tathāgata Bhaiṣajyaguru-vaiḍūryaprabharāja,
the Original Teacher Śākyamuni Tathāgata,
and all the Tathāgatas of the worlds of the ten directions.
The assembly of great Bodhisattvas and the holy multitudes who protect the Dharma gather at this place,
relying upon the sublime power of aspiration and the various karmic fruits of all the noble ones.
May there be the attainment of the most supreme, wondrous, and excellent accomplishment in accordance with the Dharma.
Furthermore, may there arise, according to each respective nature,
all kinds of superior and exquisite human and celestial requisites, food and drink, clothing, necklaces, music, and medicine, both internal and external, as desired.
Just as the *Tri-skandhaka-sūtra* describes how the ocean-like clouds of various most sublime offerings arise from the *Samantabhadra-caryā-praṇidhāna*,
so too do they transform according to one's aspirations into various kinds of ornamental requisites.
May these clouds of offerings pervade everywhere like a vast ocean.
May they be fulfilled according to one's wishes;
may it be so for the Noble Assembly as well.
"Empowerment, gathering, and joyful enjoyment"—recite this three times.
Furthermore, it says: "By the true power of the Three Jewels;
by the power of the empowerment and gathering of all Buddhas and great Bodhisattvas."
The power of the fruition of the perfection of the two types of provisions;
the inconceivable power of the pure *dharmadhātu*.
May it be accomplished according to these aspirations; may it be accomplished according to these aspirations.
Having thus performed the threefold gathering, bestowing, empowerment, and offering,
one invites all the holy beings.
Kneeling with the kneecaps on the ground, one joins the palms and holds flowers.
The invocation says:
With single-minded devotion,
I respectfully invoke the Tathāgata of Excellent Renown and Auspiciousness.
The Tathāgata Ratnacandraprajñāvyūhaghoṣeśvararāja;
the Tathāgata Suvarṇavarṇaratnābhikṣetrasiddhacaryā;
the Tathāgata Aśoka-vara-śrīrājendra.
Tathāgata Dharma-Sea Thunder-Sound;
Tathāgata Supreme Wisdom of the Dharma-Sea Sporting in Supernatural Powers;
Tathāgata Bhaiṣajyaguru Vaidūryaprabha-Rāja.
May our Teacher, Śākyamuni Tathāgata, and all the Tathāgatas,
Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas, and great Bodhisattvas of the ten directions and the three periods of time,
look upon us with compassion and mindfulness.
These World-Honored Ones, out of great kindness and great compassion,
act for the benefit of all sentient beings during the future period of the final five hundred years when the semblance Dharma prevails,
and they are obscured by the karmic obstructions of those beings.
They bring about benefit for sentient beings who are oppressed by various diseases,
constantly afflicted by grief, sorrow, suffering,
and distress, as well as those who are impoverished and in hardship.
It shall also bring benefit, peace, and happiness to humans and devas,
by virtue of the majestic power of the Tathāgatas’ skillful means and their vast, supreme, subtle, and sublime vows.
Now, for the sake of providing us— such-and-such a person— and all sentient beings with a refuge,
for the sake of providing protection, and for the sake of providing power,
we reverently invoke you: we pray that the noble assembly will deign to come.
Descend upon this ritual site, incense altar, and assembly hall.
We pray that you will grant us your compassionate protection and guidance.
With single-minded devotion, we invoke you.
Our Teacher, Śākyamuni Buddha,
for the benefit of sentient beings, has manifested the appearance of nirvāṇa in Jambudvīpa;
he will now proceed to other regions by means of the supernatural powers of a Tathāgata.
Sporting with sovereign mastery, you bring benefit and happiness to sentient beings.
We only pray that the World-Honored One, with great kindness and great compassion,
will recall your former vows and not abandon your grand resolve.
We, too, have been bound by the grace and virtue bestowed upon the sentient beings we transform;
now, for the sake of providing a refuge for all sentient beings, such-and-such a person,
we act as their protectors and provide them with power.
With sincere devotion, we invoke you.
We pray that you descend to this incense altar for our offerings.
We pray that you descend to this assembly hall and grant us your compassionate protection. With single-minded devotion, we entreat you.
The Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Mañjuśrī,
the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Trāṇamukta,
and the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi.
And to all the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and the entire assembly of noble ones:
out of great kindness and great compassion, please bear in mind this *Saptabuddhaka-pūrvapraṇidhāna-guṇa-dhāraṇī-sūtra* as it was proclaimed in the past.
At that time, before the great assembly, he made this great vow:
"In accordance with the Buddha's teachings, I shall receive and uphold the sūtras.
May all the bodhisattvas now act as a refuge for this person, [named] so-and-so, and for all sentient beings."
Because you act as a protector and because you possess great power,
I reverently invoke you.
I pray that you will descend and accept this offering at the incense altar.
I pray that you descend upon this sanctuary and grant your compassionate guidance.
With single-minded devotion, I entreat you:
in the past, at the assembly, you were personally entrusted with this mission by the Tathāgata.
"You all share the same true speech of the devas;
having received the Buddha’s command, you vow to protect the True Dharma.
May the fourfold assembly likewise vow to uphold it."
Regarding the *Saptabuddha-tathāgata-pūrvapraṇidhāna-guṇa-dharma-sūtra*:
it was [proclaimed] by Mahābrahmā, Śakra Devendra,
Dhṛtarāṣṭra Rājā, and Virūḍhaka Rājā.
The Great King Virūpākṣa, the Great King Vaiśravaṇa, and all the assemblies of holy beings who protect the Dharma:
for the sake of providing a refuge for all sentient beings, including [so-and-so],
and for the sake of providing protection and exercising power, [we pray].
I invoke you with devotion.
I pray that you descend to this incense altar for offerings;
I pray that you descend to this assembly hall and grant your compassionate protection.
With single-minded devotion,
we offer this invocation: In the presence of the Buddhas of former assemblies,
you made great vows before the great multitude.
Furthermore, if there are those who receive, uphold, read, recite, revere,
and make offerings to this *Sūtra on the Merit of the Original Vows of the Seven Tathāgatas*,
we, along with our retinues, shall protect and guard such persons.
May they cause [beings] to be liberated from all hardships and fulfill every aspiration and request.
Those who vow to provide protection and support are:
the Great General Piṅgala and the Great General Pāñcika.
The Great General Maitreya; the Great General Antira;
the Great General Anira; the Great General Sandira;
the Great General Indrāla; the Great General Paila.
General Māhura, General Candra, General Jambha,
and General Vikara— O you great generals!
One should recall the virtuous vows previously made:
that now, for the sake of providing a refuge, a protection, and a source of power for this person [named so-and-so] and all sentient beings.
I reverently invoke you.
I pray that you descend to accept these offerings of fragrant sandalwood;
may you descend to this assembly hall and grant us your compassionate protection.

At this point, one should recite the verse of invocation. Visualize that, thus invoked, the various holy beings each depart from their own lands and arrive through the air by means of their supernormal powers.
Within the supreme and wondrous palace, upon lion-throne lotus seats made of various jewels,
one should install the eight Tathāgatas and the Dharma Jewel.
On the second level, one should further install the positions of the bodhisattvas belonging to the introduction (*nidāna*).
Alternatively, one may arrange the positions of the attendant bodhisattvas,
placing Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva and Jue-tuo (Tārā) Bodhisattva before them.
The stage of the three bodhisattvas, with Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva at their head,
awakens all the deities to their past vows to perform acts of benefit.
Thirdly, on the left side, the twelve yakṣa generals are installed.
On the right side, one should install Mahābrahmā and Śakra, Lord of Devas;
at the four gates, one should install the Four Great Heavenly Kings.
In fulfillment of their former original vows, one should likewise visualize all the requisites for offering.
Contemplate and visualize according to the ritual procedures as previously described.
Next, using the water of merit and other offerings, perform prostrations and present the offering, saying:
"Namo! We take refuge in and make offerings to all the Sugatas and the assembly of great Bodhisattvas of the ten directions and the three periods of time."

Homage, refuge, and offerings to the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, King of Good Renown and Auspiciousness, together with his immeasurable hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of bodhisattvas.
Homage, refuge, and offerings to the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Sovereign King of Jewel-Moon Wisdom Adorned Radiant Sound, together with his immeasurable bodhisattvas.

Homage, refuge, and offerings to the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Buddha Accomplished in Golden Jewel Light and Sublime Conduct, together with his immeasurable hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of bodhisattvas.
Homage and refuge to the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Aśoka-vara-śrī-rāja Buddha and his immeasurable assembly of bodhisattvas;
homage and refuge to the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Dharmasāgara-nirghoṣa Buddha and his immeasurable assembly of bodhisattvas;
homage and refuge to the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Dharmasāgara-jñānavikrīḍita-abhijña Buddha and his immeasurable assembly of bodhisattvas.

Homage, refuge, and offerings to the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Bhaisajyaguru-vaiḍūryaprabharāja Buddha, to the Sunlight-pervading and Moonlight-pervading Buddhas, and to the assembly of immeasurable bodhisattvas.
Homage, refuge, and offerings to the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, our Teacher Śākyamuni Buddha, and to the assembly of thirty-six thousand bodhisattvas.
Homage, refuge, and offerings to Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva, Jie-duo (Trātar) Bodhisattva, Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva, and the assembly of all great bodhisattvas.
Homage and refuge to the Great Brahmā Deva King, the Lord Śakra, the Four Great Heavenly Kings, and the assembly of holy sages who protect the Dharma;
homage and refuge to the General Piṇḍola Bhāradvāja and the assembly of the twelve Yakṣas.
Next, the offering is presented as follows: "Before all the Great Sages,
I now offer this water of wondrous merit,
along with unguents, exquisite flowers, burning incense, and bright lamps."
Exquisite food, music, and subtle sounds;
banners, pennants, parasols, and all manner of ritual implements for offering;
as well as all the various things throughout the worlds of the ten directions that are not held by any owner.
With the sublime and exquisite requisites for the sensual pleasures of humans and devas,
and further through the power of the great vidyā-mantras of dhāraṇī, as well as the power of sincere faith and aspiration,
may these clouds of offerings be empowered and increased like a vast ocean.
Furthermore, as produced from the *Samantabhadra-caryā-praṇidhāna*,
clouds of offerings fill the expanse of space;
such are these most supreme requisites for making offerings.
I offer this to the assembly of all great holy ones. I,
[Name], and others, from beginningless time within the cycle of birth and death until now,
have committed all manner of evil and sinful karmic deeds.
Furthermore, regarding the various unwholesome karmas— both those I should have done but did not,
and those I should not have done but did— I now truly and completely repent of all such sinful deeds.
I rejoice in all roots of virtue belonging to the Buddhas of the three periods of time and to all sentient beings.
All Tathāgatas of the ten directions—
I now entreat you to turn the Great Wheel of Dharma.
To all those lamps of the world who desire to enter parinirvāṇa,
I now entreat you not to enter nirvāṇa.
May you remain long in this world for the benefit and happiness of sentient beings.
Thus, O Blessed One, may the noble assembly gathered here deign to take pity upon me.
These World-Honored Ones, out of great kindness and great compassion,
act for the benefit of all sentient beings during the final five hundred years of the Semblance Dharma,
when they are shrouded by the karmic obstructions of their own deeds.
They bring about benefit for sentient beings who are oppressed by various diseases,
constantly afflicted by sorrow, lamentation, suffering,
and distress, as well as those who are impoverished and in hardship.
It is also for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of humans and devas.
This is the skillful means employed by those seven Tathāgatas, the World-Honored Ones,
the Arhats, the Samyaksaṃbuddhas, in their assemblies of the past.
The empowerment and sustaining grace of the great, most supreme, and subtle vows were bestowed;
our Teacher, Śākyamuni Buddha, likewise proclaimed this sutra and bestowed empowerment and sustaining grace.
Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva,
Rakṣa-paritrāṇa Bodhisattva,
and the assembly of Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas.
Truly accomplishing the noble speech spoken by that Buddha, the World-Honored One,
they fulfill their respective great original vows and also bring to completion the purpose and benefit of this sutra.
Having accomplished all the noble ones, he delivered the sacred words of entrustment.
He empowered and sustained Mahābrahmā, Śakra Devendra,
the Four Great Kings, and the twelve yakṣas.
The assembly of noble Dharma-protectors and upāsakas formerly made great vows at this assembly to guard and protect this sutra and those who uphold it.
Therefore, we too shall proclaim the ritual procedures for the merits of our original vows, just as the noble ones have done;
we shall construct a maṇḍala and assemble the ocean-like assembly of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.
Various articles for making offerings have been arranged;
we extol the holy names and present these offerings.
Now, having received your bestowed grace, we have gathered at this site of practice.
I prostrate and pray that all the sages will graciously bestow their benevolence and virtue, mindful of their great vows,
to bring this assembly’s *maṇḍala* to completion.
May it likewise be so for me, [Name], and all sentient beings.
"Behold how one obtains the merits and benefits as described in the sūtras"— thus it is said three times.
Furthermore, one should offer worship to each of the noble ones (ārya) individually, making aspirations and prayers.
First, recite the name of the Tathāgata Bhagavān Śubhavyūha-śrī-rāja Buddha and present various offerings while making this prayer:
"Namo! I take refuge in, and pay homage to, the Bhagavān Tathāgata Arhat Samyaksaṃbuddha Śubhavyūha-śrī-rāja Buddha. Recite this seven times.

Next, I prostrate and offer worship: Now, before the presence of all Buddhas and the assembly of great Bodhisattvas and holy ones, if one hears the name of the Tathāgata Bhadraśrīkīrtirāja Buddha, [one shall attain...]
With right mindfulness, one contemplates and extols the holy name;
through the majestic power of sevenfold respectful offerings and prostrations,
it shall be just as the supreme vows originally made by the Tathāgata King of Good Renown and Auspiciousness.
May we and all sentient beings be spared from all bodily afflictions caused by illness— such as fevers,
various types of malaria, parasites, malevolent spells, and the raising of corpses— as well as from other such torments.
Afflicted by various forms of fear and harm,
we pray that until we attain unsurpassed bodhi,
all such calamities and the suffering of illness may [be pacified].
May they all be extinguished; may they be entirely extinguished.
Furthermore, may we and all sentient beings be freed from all varieties of blindness, deafness, and muteness.
From leprosy, insanity, and the afflictions of various diseases,
we pray that until we realize unsurpassed bodhi,
all our sensory faculties may be complete and free from every illness and suffering.
May they be completely extinguished.
Furthermore, may we and all sentient beings be freed from the entanglements of greed, hatred, and delusion.
Having committed the crimes of immediate retribution and various evil deeds,
slandering the true Dharma and failing to cultivate manifold virtues,
they shall fall into the hells and other evil realms to undergo all manner of suffering.
We pray that all such five crimes of immediate retribution as we have committed,
along with all karmic obstructions, may be completely extinguished,
until we attain unsurpassed bodhi.
May we no longer fall into the paths of the three evil realms,
but constantly experience the sublime happiness of humans and devas.
Furthermore, I pray that we and all sentient beings—
All manner of poverty and suffering,
such as a lack of clothing, food, necklaces,
bedding, wealth, treasures, incense, flowers, and music.
May we, until we attain unsurpassed bodhi,
[be provided with] all clothing, food, necklaces,
bedding, wealth, treasures, incense, flowers, and music.
May all their livelihoods be prosperous, abundant, and sufficient.
Furthermore, may we and all sentient beings,
even if our bodies are bound by shackles and fetters or subjected to flogging, [be liberated].
We undergo various sufferings and afflictions;
may we, until we attain unsurpassed bodhi,
be freed from all such manifold bondages, lashings, and every form of suffering and affliction.
May they all attain liberation and be entirely extinguished.
Furthermore, may we and all sentient beings be freed from the oppression of the fires of suffering—
those various states that are without rescue and without refuge.
In perilous places, they are harassed by various predatory beasts— bears, brown bears, lions, tigers, leopards, jackals, wolves, vipers, snakes, and scorpions—
who seek to end their lives and inflict upon them great suffering.
May we, until we attain unsurpassed bodhi,
be liberated from all terrors;
may all predatory beasts give rise to a heart of compassion and always find peace and happiness.
Furthermore, may we and all sentient beings be free from the various forms of mutual combat, verbal disputes,
and arguments that give rise to sorrow, affliction, alarm, and fear.
May we, until we attain unsurpassed bodhi,
have all various words of contention dissolved,
and may all fear and suffering be dispelled.
May all [hostilities] be completely extinguished so that we may face one another with hearts of loving-kindness.
Furthermore, may we and all sentient beings,
when entering rivers or oceans for the sake of sustaining our lives, [be free from harm].
Encountering a great and violent wind that blew their ship, they found no island or shore upon which to take refuge; overcome with extreme distress, they made this vow:
"May we, until we attain unsurpassed bodhi, [be protected]."
Free from all fears, may we attain everything according to our wishes and reach a place of peace and security to enjoy all forms of happiness.
Furthermore, may we, upon the end of this life, [be reborn there].
One will immediately attain rebirth among the people of the kingdom of the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Śrīkīrtirāja.
There, one will be born by transformation upon a lotus flower atop a lion throne made of various jewels.
They have realized all the merits of various *dhāraṇī* gates and *samādhi* gates,
and [they pay homage] to their venerable teacher, the Tathāgata King of Excellent Renown and Auspiciousness, as well as to the Buddhas of the ten directions.
Hearing the sublime Dharma and making offerings and service, he was graced by the Buddha’s joy for a brief moment and attained unhindered entry into all buddha-fields.
*Namo*—homage, refuge, and offerings to the Bhagavān, Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Ratnacandraprajñāvyūhaprabhasvararāja Buddha. (Recite thus seven times.)

Next, I proffer this offering and so forth: now, before the presence of the Buddhas and the assembly of great Bodhisattvas, if one hears the name of the Buddha Ratnacandraprabhatejobhyudgatarāja, [one shall attain such merit].
With right mindfulness, contemplate and recite the holy name;
through the majestic spiritual power of sevenfold respectful offerings and prostrations,
it shall be just like that of the Buddha Ratnacandraprabhāsa-śrī-tejo-rāja-svatantra.
I have made this most excellent, subtle,
and supreme aspiration: may all of us sentient beings,
for the sake of engaging in agriculture and commerce, [attain success].
Delighting in and becoming attached to them causes the mind to be disturbed and leads to the neglect of the sublime, virtuous dharmas for awakening.
One falls into the cycle of birth and death and is unable to escape,
undergoing individually the immeasurable and boundless sufferings of old age, sickness, death, grief, lamentation, and affliction.
We pray that until we attain unsurpassed bodhi,
our clothing, food and drink, and all necessities of life,
as well as gold, silver, and precious jewels, may be fully provided according to our wishes.
All roots of goodness shall increase;
they shall never abandon the bodhicitta,
and they shall all obtain liberation from the sufferings of the evil realms.
Furthermore, may we and all sentient beings,
if we are oppressed by cold, heat, hunger, or thirst and experience great physical suffering and distress—
may we, indeed, may this very body [be so transformed].
From their final birth until they realize unsurpassed bodhi,
all their karmic offenses from previous lives will be completely extinguished;
they will cast off all suffering and affliction to enjoy the bliss of humans and devas.
Furthermore, may we and all sentient beings—
should there be women whose bodies and minds are oppressed by various sufferings and who consequently give rise to revulsion— [attain liberation].
And at the time of childbirth, one undergoes great suffering and distress;
may all such various sufferings and distresses be completely extinguished.
Furthermore, may I be born as my final birth.
Until the attainment of unsurpassed bodhi, may we always be male.
Furthermore, may we and all sentient beings [be born] together with our parents, brothers, and sisters.
May my wife, children, kinsmen, and all my friends—
who are beset by thieves and afflicted by various sufferings while traveling through perilous places—
be spared from harm; and may we, until we attain unsurpassed bodhi, [be likewise protected].
May all those who suffer from being plundered by bandits in dangerous and perilous places be liberated from all hardships and may their afflictions be extinguished.
Furthermore, may we and all sentient beings,
when performing various activities during the darkness of night,
be free from the afflictions and disturbances of malevolent spirits and ghosts, and be spared the arising of extreme sorrow and suffering.
We pray that until we attain unsurpassed bodhi,
all such evil hardships may transition from darkness to light,
and that all malevolent spirits and deities may give rise to thoughts of compassion.
I shall exert great diligence to serve and make offerings.
Furthermore, I vow that myself and all sentient beings may refrain from committing base and evil deeds and place no faith in the Triple Gem.
Lacking wisdom, we have not cultivated wholesome dharmas;
we have failed to practice the faculties, powers, factors of awakening, mindfulness, concentration, and dhāraṇī.
We pray only that we may continue until we realize unsurpassed bodhi.
As their wisdom gradually increased,
they developed deep faith in the Triple Gem and practiced all thirty-seven factors of enlightenment (*bodhipākṣika-dharma*).
Furthermore, they made this aspiration for themselves and all sentient beings:
With inferior intentions, we abide in the practice of the paths of the two vehicles.
We turn our backs on unsurpassed, supreme, and wondrous bodhi.
May it be that we shall [not do so] until we have attained unsurpassed bodhi.
Mindfully recollecting the bodhicitta, one abandons the views of the two vehicles and attains non-retrogression from unsurpassed enlightenment.
Furthermore, may we and all sentient beings [attain this].
When they see the end of the eon approaching and the fires about to arise in Jambudvīpa and other realms,
they give rise to great anxiety, fear, suffering, and lamentation,
due to the power of the evil karma of their previous lives.
Suffering these manifold pains with no one to turn to for refuge,
we pray only that until we attain unsurpassed bodhi,
such sorrow and suffering may all be extinguished and we may experience the bliss of cool serenity.
Furthermore, may we, upon the end of this life,
immediately attain rebirth within the land of the Buddha Ratnacandravimalaprabhāsvaramaheśvararāja.
May we be born by transformation upon lotus flowers atop lion thrones made of various precious gems.
He attained all the merits of various *dhāraṇīs*, vidyās, and samādhi-gates;
furthermore, he [saw] the Teacher, the Tathāgata Ratnacandraprajñāvyūhaprabhasvararāja, and the Tathāgatas of the ten directions.
Having heard the sublime Dharma and rendered service and offerings, he was graced by the Buddha’s joy for a brief moment.

He attained unhindered entry into all buddha-fields. *Namo*—homage, refuge, and offerings to the Bhagavān, Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Suvarṇavarṇaratnābhakāryasampanna Buddha. (Recite this seven times.)

Next, I proffer these offerings and so forth: now, before the presence of the assembly of all Buddhas and great Bodhisattvas, if one hears the name of the Tathāgata Golden-Colored Jewel Light Wondrous Practice Accomplishment, [one shall attain such benefits].
With right mindfulness, one should contemplate and extol the holy name,
reverently making offerings and prostrating seven times; by the power of this majestic spiritual authority,
it shall be just like the Tathāgata Suvarṇavarṇaprabhāsa-sucaritābhyudgata.
Regarding the most supreme, subtle, and exalted vows we have made:
may we and all sentient beings who have committed various acts of slaughter and violence, taking the lives of others, [be purified].
Due to these evil karmas, they undergo the sufferings of hell;

even if they obtain a human birth, they will have short lifespans and many illnesses, or be wounded by water, fire, blades, or poisons, and must endure the suffering of death. We pray that we may, until we attain unsurpassed bodhi, [be spared from such fates].
May all evil karma be completely extinguished;
may we be free from illness and enjoy long life, never meeting with untimely death.
Furthermore, I pray that we and all sentient beings [may attain these blessings].
By committing various evil deeds and seizing property by force,
or by stealing wealth and goods, one shall fall into the evil realms;
even if one obtains birth as a human, it will be into a poor family.
Lacking food and clothing, we constantly endure hardship and suffering.
We pray that until we attain unsurpassed bodhi,
all our evil karma may be completely extinguished.
May there be no lack of clothing, food, or drink;
may we obtain abundance.
Furthermore, may it be so for ourselves and all sentient beings.
May all sentient beings cease their mutual contempt and arrogance,
and may they no longer harbor enmity or engage in reciprocal killing and harm.
We pray that we may attain unsurpassed bodhi.
May such suffering and affliction be extinguished.
May you each give rise to compassion for us as if we were your own parents.
Furthermore, may it be so for ourselves and all sentient beings.
All sentient beings— whether householders or renunciants, men or women of the seven assemblies— are entangled and obscured by various forms of greed, hatred, and delusion,
and thus they violate the precepts established by the Tathāgata.
Having committed various evil deeds while receiving the offerings of the faithful in vain,
we shall fall into hell to undergo various bitter retributions.
We pray only that we may continue until the attainment of unsurpassed bodhi.
All evil karma shall be completely extinguished.
Severing all afflictions, one reverently upholds the *śīla* (precepts),
skillfully guarding body, speech, and mind, never to regress.

*Vaiśvati namaḥ sarvatathāgatānāṃ svāhā*. This is that Blessed One, the Tathāgata,
Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, the Buddha of Golden Jewel Light and the Accomplishment of Wondrous Conduct.
Seated beneath the Bodhi tree, he beheld sentient beings entangled by greed,
hatred, and delusion, oppressed by manifold ailments,
vulnerable to enemies, and sometimes meeting with untimely death.
Furthermore, due to their evil karma, they fall into the hells and undergo extreme suffering.
For the sake of benefiting these afflicted sentient beings,
and to eliminate their karmic obstructions so that they may ultimately abide in unsurpassed enlightenment, [I shall practice].
Having spoken this divine mantra,
through the power of our sincere recitation and upholding of this mantra,
we pray that we and all sentient beings—
All extremely grave offenses of the five deeds of immediate retribution,
as well as all karmic obstructions, shall be completely extinguished.
All that is sought after shall be ultimately and perfectly fulfilled.
At the time of death, one shall behold that World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Golden Radiance Wondrous Conduct Accomplishment, who will protect and mindfully regard one with compassion.
Upon passing away from this life, one shall immediately attain rebirth within the Buddha-land of that Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, the Golden Radiance Wondrous Conduct Accomplishment.
Upon lion thrones of various precious lotuses, they are born through transformation from the lotuses,
attaining all merits such as the various *dhāraṇī* gates and *samādhi* gates.
Furthermore, they heard the sublime Dharma from the Guide, the Tathāgata Suvarṇavarṇaratnābhācārasamudgata, as well as from the Tathāgatas of the ten directions;
they served and made offerings to them,
and having received the Buddhas' favor, they remained for a brief moment.
May I enter all Buddha-fields without obstruction.
Homage and refuge to the Bhagavān, Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Aśoka-vara-śrī-rāja Buddha. (Recite this seven times.)

Next, I proffer these offerings and so forth: now, before the presence of the Buddhas, the great Bodhisattvas, and the assembly of holy ones, if one hears the name of the Buddha King of Supreme Auspiciousness Free from Sorrow, [one shall attain...]
With right mindfulness, contemplate and recite the holy name;
through sevenfold reverent offerings and prostrations, by the power of his majestic spiritual authority,
he shall be just like the Tathāgata Aśoka-vara-śrī-rāja.
This most excellent resolve is like a sublime and supreme aspiration:
may we and all sentient beings never again be constantly tormented and oppressed by sorrow and suffering.
We pray that until we attain unsurpassed bodhi,
all our grief, sorrow, and various afflictions may be completely extinguished; furthermore,
may we never suffer the pain of separation from those we love, but instead enjoy long life and peace and security.
Furthermore, may we and all sentient beings who have committed various evil karmas and are born in the dark places of the great hells,
suffering all manner of agonies, [be liberated].
May we, through being touched by the light from the body of the Tathāgata Aśoka-vara-śrī-rāja,
have all our karmic obstructions completely extinguished,
until we realize unsurpassed bodhi.
May they be liberated from all sufferings and be born among humans and devas to experience happiness as they wish.
Furthermore, may we and all sentient beings [be purified of] the various evil karmas of killing, stealing, and sexual misconduct.
In this present life, they will experience the suffering of being struck by blades and staves;
in the future, they will fall into the evil destinies.
Even if they should obtain a human body, it will be short-lived and plagued by many illnesses, and they will be born into a family of poverty and low status.
Their clothing, food, and drink are entirely lacking;
they constantly endure the sufferings of cold, heat, hunger, and thirst.
Their bodies lack a radiant luster, and the retinues they attract are none of them virtuous or noble.
May we, until we attain unsurpassed bodhi,
have all our needs for food, drink, and clothing fully satisfied according to our wishes;
and may we possess lovely physical radiance and excellent retinues, just like those gods.
Furthermore, may we and all sentient beings,
should we be harassed by yakṣas or various malevolent spirits who steal our vital essence and cause us to suffer from manifold diseases and afflictions, [be liberated].
May we, until we attain unsurpassed bodhi,
cause all malevolent yakṣas and spirits to disperse and each give rise to a heart of loving-kindness.
The vital essence that was stolen shall be restored to its original state,
and all suffering from illness shall be completely liberated.
Furthermore, we pray that from this point until the end of our lives, [we may...]
One will immediately attain rebirth within the land of the Buddha King of Supreme Auspiciousness Free from Sorrow,
where one will be born by transformation upon a lotus flower atop a lion throne made of various jewels.
They have realized all the merits of various *dhāraṇī* gates and *samādhi* gates;
furthermore, regarding the Teacher, the Most Victorious Auspicious King Free from Sorrow (*Aśoka-vara-śrī-rāja-tathāgata*), and the Tathāgatas of the ten directions.
Hearing the sublime Dharma and making offerings and service, one receives the Buddha’s joy for a brief moment and enters all buddha-fields without obstruction.
*Namo*—I take refuge in and make offerings to the Bhagavān Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Dharmasāgaragarjitasvara Buddha. (Recite this seven times.)
Next, I prostrate and offer worship: now, before the presence of the Buddhas and the assembly of great Bodhisattvas,
if one hears the name of the Buddha Dharma-Sea-Thunder-Sound,
one should contemplate it with right mindfulness and extol his holy name.
Through the majestic power of reverently making offerings and prostrating seven times,
it is also like the most supreme, subtle, and sublime vows issued by the Tathāgata Dharmasāgaragarjitasvara.
May we and all sentient beings,
should we be born into families of wrong views where no pure faith arises toward the Buddha,
Dharma, and Sangha, [be spared from such rebirth].
May we remain far removed from the thought of supreme enlightenment;
rather, we pray that until we attain supreme enlightenment,
our ignorance and false wisdom may be eliminated day and night.
May we develop profound and correct faith in the Triple Gem and never again regress from the mind set upon unsurpassed bodhi.
Furthermore, may we and all sentient beings [attain this].
Born in a remote borderland,
they associate with evil friends, commit various sinful deeds, and do not cultivate wholesome qualities;
the very names of the Triple Gem have never reached their ears.
After their lives have ended, they will fall into the three evil realms;
yet those sentient beings shall, for a brief moment, hear the name of the Tathāgata Dharma-ocean Thunder-voice,
and also hear the sounds of the Dharma-cloud and the Dharma-ocean.
Having heard this sound of the Dharma,
we pray that we and all sentient beings may,
until we attain unsurpassed bodhi, [be sustained by it].
All such karmic obstructions will be eliminated;
one will encounter spiritual friends and not fall into the evil destinies,
and shall never forsake the bodhicitta.
Furthermore, may we and all sentient beings lack nothing that is required for our livelihood—
be it clothing, food and drink, bedding, medicine,
or any other necessities.
Due to these causes and conditions, great sorrow and suffering arise; because of seeking [what we desire], we commit manifold evil karmas.
We pray that until we realize unsurpassed bodhi, [may this be so].
May clothing, food and drink, bedding, medicine,
and all necessities of life be obtained at will upon mere thought, without anything being lacking.
Furthermore, may we and all sentient beings [attain this].
Due to our past evil karma, we have engaged in mutual strife and contention,
inflicting harm upon one another with bows, arrows, swords,
and staves. We pray that all of us sentient beings...
Until they attain unsurpassed bodhi,
they shall not harm one another with swords or staves,
but shall each give rise to a mind of loving-kindness and refrain from mutual injury.
All unwholesome thoughts shall completely disperse;
they shall not arise within oneself, much less toward others.
One should constantly practice joy and renunciation, desiring to sever the [karmic] causes for taking life.
Regarding each of our various requisites and articles of enjoyment,
may we give rise to a mind of contentment and no longer cause disturbance or encroachment.
Furthermore, we pray that after we pass away from this life, [we may be reborn in the Pure Land].
One will immediately attain rebirth within the buddha-land of the Buddha Dharma-Sāgara-Garjita-Svara. There,
one will be born by transformation upon a lotus flower on a lion throne made of various jewels,
and will realize all merits, including various *dhāraṇī* gates and *samādhi* gates.
Furthermore, he heard the sublime Dharma from the Tathāgatas of the ten directions, including the Teacher Dharmasāgaragarjitasvara Tathāgata;
he served and made offerings to them,
and having received the Buddhas' favor, he remained for a brief moment.

Translated by the Tripitaka Master Śaraba, a śramaṇa of the Great Yuan, by Imperial Decree. Namo Bhaiṣajyaguru-vaiḍūryaprabharāja Tathāgata. Namo to the Bhagavat, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Dharmasāgaravijayamati-vikrīḍita-abhijña Buddha. [Recite thus seven times.]

Next, I prostrate and offer worship: Now, before the presence of the Buddhas, the great Bodhisattvas, and the assembly of holy ones, if one hears the name of the Buddha *Dharmasāgaravijayamatigatirvikrīḍitābhijña*.
With right mindfulness, contemplate and recite the holy name;
through the majestic power of sevenfold respectful offerings and prostrations,
it shall likewise be as the most supreme, subtle, and sublime vow originally made by the Tathāgata Dharmasāgaravijayagatiguṇaviśuddhivikrīḍitabhijña.
May we and all sentient beings—
those who have committed various evil deeds, who have plowed and tilled, causing harm to living beings,
or who have engaged in trade and deceived others— [be purified].
In battle arrays and amidst weapons, we are constantly subjected to slaughter.
We pray that we may,
until we attain unsurpassed bodhi, [be spared from such harm].
May the necessities of life be provided without the need for seeking or striving, and may they be fulfilled according to one's heart's desire.
Furthermore, may we and all sentient beings be purified of the ten non-virtuous actions, such as the sins of killing and so forth.
Due to these causes and conditions, we shall fall into hell.
We pray that until we realize unsurpassed bodhi,
we may fully accomplish the ten paths of wholesome action and never fall into the evil realms.
Furthermore, may we and all sentient beings not fall under the power of others,
becoming their dependents,
nor be bound by fetters, shackles, manacles, or stocks.
From the infliction of whips and staves up to the most extreme punishments,
we pray that we may attain unsurpassed bodhi even through our speech,
and that we may be liberated from all calamities, imprisonment, and flogging.
May they attain mastery, majestic power, and fulfillment.
Furthermore, may we and all sentient beings who have committed various evil deeds and possess short lifespans [be liberated from them].
Throughout all times, they shall not meet with untimely death;
and at the moment of their passing, they shall for a brief instant hear the name of the Tathāgata Dharmasāgaravijayasamudgata-vikrīḍita-abhijña.
With right mindfulness present before us, may we be liberated from all hardships;
may we always be born in the Central Land and experience supreme, wondrous bliss.
We pray that this shall continue until we realize unsurpassed bodhi.
May we forever be free from all calamities and always enjoy the sublime and wondrous bliss of gods and humans.
Furthermore, may we, upon passing away from this life,
immediately attain rebirth within the Buddha-land of the Tathāgata Dharmasāgaraviśeṣamati-vikrīḍita-abhijña.
Upon lion thrones of various precious lotuses,
they were born through transformation from the lotuses,
having realized all merits, including various *dhāraṇī* gates and *samādhi* gates.
Furthermore, from the Tathāgata Dharmasāgaravijayamati-vikrīḍita-abhijña, the Teacher, as well as from the Tathāgatas of the ten directions,
he heard the sublime Dharma, served and made offerings to them, and was graced by the Buddhas' joy.

In an instant, one enters all Buddha-fields without obstruction. Homage, refuge, and offerings to the Bhagavān, Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Bhaiṣajyaguruvaidūryaprabharāja Buddha—recite this seven times.

Next, the offerings and so forth are presented: Now, before the presence of the Buddhas and the assembly of great Bodhisattvas and holy ones, if one hears the name of the Buddha Bhaiṣajyaguru-vaiḍūryaprabha-rāja, [one shall obtain such benefits].
With right mindfulness, one should contemplate and chant the holy name;
through the majestic spiritual power of sevenfold respectful offerings and prostrations,
it shall be just like the most supreme, subtle, and sublime vows originally made by the Tathāgata Bhaiṣajyaguru-vaiḍūryaprabha-rāja.
May we and all sentient beings adorn our bodies with the thirty-two marks of a great man and the eighty secondary signs,
so that they are radiant and blazing with light.
It illuminates immeasurable and boundless worlds.
We pray that we may likewise cause all sentient beings to be exactly thus, without any difference.
Furthermore, may we and all sentient beings have bodies like lapis lazuli, transparent both inside and out,
pure and free from blemish, with vast and expansive radiance.
With majestic merit, his body dwells in perfect stability;
adorned with a net of flames, he surpasses the sun and moon.
We pray that we and all sentient beings may likewise attain this.
Until they attain unsurpassed bodhi,
they will be no different from the Tathāgata Bhaisajyaguru-vaiḍūryaprabha-rāja.
All sentient beings in the dark realms will receive illumination and understanding, and will be able to see one another.
May they carry out all activities according to their inclinations.
Furthermore, may we and all sentient beings be like that Tathāgata,
the Medicine Master Vaidūryaprabharāja.
Furthermore, through immeasurable wisdom and skillful means,
may you cause us and all sentient beings to eventually realize unexcelled bodhi.
May all obtain inexhaustible objects for their enjoyment,
so that no sentient being shall lack anything.
Furthermore, may we and all sentient beings who wander upon wrong paths [attain liberation].
May we and all sentient beings,
until we attain unsurpassed bodhi,
all be established securely upon the true path to enlightenment.
If there are those who practice the inferior vehicles of the Śrāvakas or Pratyekabuddhas,
may I establish them all in the Great Vehicle through my vows.
Furthermore, may I and all sentient beings [attain this].
Within the Buddha-dharma, they practice the holy life,
causing all to attain unimpaired precepts and skillfully guarding the three karmas so that there is no transgression.
We pray that until we attain unsurpassed bodhi,
even if we should commit transgressions, we may regain purity and not fall into the evil realms.
Furthermore, we pray for ourselves and all sentient beings.
They were deficient in their sense faculties, ugly, dull, and foolish;
blind, deaf, mute, crippled, lame, and hunchbacked;
afflicted and oppressed by various diseases and sufferings such as leprosy and insanity.
May we and all sentient beings,
until we attain unsurpassed bodhi,
have all our illnesses and sufferings completely extinguished.
May they be endowed with all faculties, be dignified and wise;
furthermore, may we and all sentient beings who are impoverished,
afflicted by suffering, and without refuge or protection [be so endowed].
Without physician, without medicine, without kin, and without home;
may we and all sentient beings,
until we attain unsurpassed bodhi, [be protected].
May all illnesses be eliminated, may our retinues flourish, and may we never lack material resources; may body and mind be peaceful and happy.
Furthermore, I pray that we and all sentient beings [may attain these blessings].
Afflicted by the hundred evils of the female body,
we feel extreme revulsion and vow to relinquish this female form.
We pray that we, along with all sentient beings, may [be liberated].
Until the attainment of unsurpassed bodhi,
may all of us transform our female bodies into male ones and possess the physical marks of a man.
Furthermore, I pray that we and all sentient beings—
Bound by the snares of Māra and various non-Buddhist paths,
and having fallen into the dense forest of manifold evil views,
we pray that we and all sentient beings may [be liberated].
Until they attain unsurpassed bodhi,
you shall always provide them with guidance and protection, causing them to distance themselves from false views and give rise to right view,
gradually leading them to cultivate all the practices of a bodhisattva.
May we swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
Furthermore, may we and all sentient beings,
even when bound by royal law and confined within prisons, [attain this realization].
There are shackles, flogging, and even the ultimate punishments;
furthermore, there are many other forms of suffering.
One is coerced and tormented, with not a moment's respite from joy.
May we and all sentient beings,
until we attain unsurpassed bodhi,
rely upon the Buddha’s majestic power so that all sorrows and sufferings may be completely liberated.
Furthermore, may we and all sentient beings, tormented by the fires of hunger and driven to commit various evil deeds for the sake of seeking food,
[be liberated]; may we and all sentient beings [attain peace].
Until they attain unsurpassed bodhi,
by relying on the Buddha’s majestic power, they shall all obtain exquisite food and drink,
becoming fully satiated according to their wishes.
Furthermore, may they find peace and happiness through the flavor of the Dharma.
Moreover, I pray that I and all sentient beings shall not be afflicted by the lack of clothing, nor by mosquitoes, insects, cold, or heat.
May we and all sentient beings,
until the attainment of unsurpassed bodhi,
rely upon the Buddha’s majestic power to fulfill our respective aspirations.
They immediately obtained various kinds of exquisite garments,
precious ornaments, fragrant flowers, and musical performances;
all were made joyful and satisfied, becoming abundantly provided for and free from all suffering and affliction.
Furthermore, may they be fully endowed with the precepts received from the Noble Ones;
may they remain far removed from the oppression of afflictions;
and may they dwell long in the peace and happiness of universal liberation.
Upon passing away from this life, they will immediately attain rebirth within the land of the Buddha Bhaisajyaguru-vaidūryaprabharāja,
where they will be born by transformation upon lotus flowers atop lion thrones made of various jewels.
They have realized all the merits of various *dhāraṇī* gates and *samādhi* gates,
and furthermore, [they have taken refuge] in the Teacher, the Tathāgata Bhaiṣajyaguru-vaiḍūryaprabha-rāja, and the Tathāgatas of the ten directions.
Having heard the sublime Dharma and rendered service and offerings, may I receive the Buddha’s joy.

if one hears the name of Śākyamuni Buddha,
one should contemplate it with right mindfulness and extol this holy name.

our Teacher Śākyamuni Buddha acts for the benefit of all sentient beings of the future who are shrouded by karmic obstructions.
